requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.summary: MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException when collecting a closed generic value type declared in a referenced assembly. The crash prevents source generation and leaves the consuming app without GeneratedMessagePackResolver; the requested outcome is a clean build with the resolver generated.

criteria.text: Building `app` in the supplied two-project repro, where `lib` declares generic `record struct Item<T>` and `app` uses `Item<int>` as a member type through a `ProjectReference`, completes without CS8785 or an IndexOutOfRangeException from MessagePackGenerator.
criteria.summary: Repro builds with cross-project Item<int>, without CS8785 or generator crashes

criteria.text: Building that repro does not produce AD0001 caused by MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
criteria.summary: Build produces no AD0001 from analyzer IndexOutOfRangeException

criteria.text: The MessagePack generator contributes output for `app`, and the built `app.dll` contains `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.
criteria.summary: Generator output includes GeneratedMessagePackResolver in built app.dll

criteria.text: The crash-free behavior also applies when the referenced generic value type is declared as plain `struct Item<T>` rather than `record struct Item<T>`, without moving it into `app` or adding a custom formatter.
criteria.summary: Plain struct Item<T> also builds across projects without custom formatter

criteria.text: The GetObjectInfo collection and diagnostic path reached for a closed generic metadata value type handles an empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences collection without indexing element 0 or throwing.
criteria.summary: GetObjectInfo handles empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences without indexing or throwing

requirement.short: MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer must generate GeneratedMessagePackResolver for referenced closed generic value types

hunks.context: Two assembly-level attributes exist to help with mixing in your own custom forma
lines: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

+Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
+Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
+This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
+Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

claims.statement: The MsgPack004 documentation says the analyzer reports only members declared in the current project and that an unattributed public member from a referenced assembly must be fixed in its defining project.
claims.summary: MsgPack004 documentation directs referenced assembly member fixes to defining projects

claims.statement: The three new tests compile a defining source file to a metadata-only assembly, run the consuming source with that reference and no expected diagnostics, then run MessagePackGenerator separately and assert both no warning-or-error generator diagnostics and the expected resolver hint name. The cases cover a keyed plain generic struct, a keyed generic record struct, and a plain generic struct with an unkeyed public property.
claims.summary: Tests cover metadata-only generic structs, clean diagnostics, and resolver hints

facts: No file of the runtime library (src/MessagePack/), which deserializes untrusted input, is changed.
No project, package or build file is changed.

suspicions.hypothesis: The tests do not establish that app builds successfully or that app.dll contains GeneratedMessagePackResolver: they assert a generator hint name but never run RunGeneratorsAndUpdateCompilation, emit the consuming compilation, or inspect the emitted assembly. An emit failure or omitted resolver type could therefore coexist with passing tests.

The documentation's premise that the defining assembly reports metadata-member diagnostics is untested and can be false: CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync emits the library without running the analyzers, and a prebuilt dependency may never be analyzed at all.

None of the new test inputs exercises the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull branch changed in H4—all keys are ordinary integer keys or absent—so an error specific to the new property-location helper or its metadata input could remain undetected.

A previously valid analyzer diagnostic deliberately created at Location.None will now be silently lost even when it concerns a source type in the current compilation; a regression test with such a diagnostic would distinguish the broad filtering behavior from the metadata-member fix.

probes.title: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops Location.None diagnostics from source members
probes.hypothesis: C1 wraps every diagnostic through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation; since Location.None has IsInSource == false, any legitimate analyzer diagnostic deliberately created at Location.None for a source type (e.g. MyObject) is silently dropped. The requirement does not ask for this broad filtering — it asks only to avoid indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]. A test that has a source member with both Key and StringKey null and expects MsgPack004-style feedback through the diagnostic callback should observe no diagnostic reported at head.
criteria: A TypeCollector constructed against a source MyObject with a property that has neither Key nor StringKey (so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull fires) forwards the diagnostic to the callback; at head ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops it only if Location is None, which GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns for source properties? No — it returns the identifier location for source PropertyDeclarationSyntax. So the diagnostic is preserved. This probe confirms the wrapper is too broad only if the diagnostic Location is None. Instead test that any unrelated AnalyzerException must not silently be swallowed.
probes.means: If this test passes, the broad wrapper in H6 does not swallow the source-member diagnostic path. If it FAILS with 'expected diagnostic not found' or 'actual diagnostics are ... None', that confirms C1's ReportIfLocatedInCompilation silently drops legitimate diagnostics because a caller supplied Location.None or a syntax tree mismatch, which the requirement does not ask for.

rounds.reason: /root/wt/2283-probe-P1/tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/ProbeMsPack2283DiagnosticReporting.cs(55,38): error CS0103: The name 'MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer' does not exist in the current context [/root/wt/2283-probe-P1/tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests.

The probe fails identically at base and head with VerifyCS's "Expected source file list to match" error, not with a missing MsgPack004 diagnostic. It also uses a member-located diagnostic rather than exercising the hypothesized Location.None filtering. The failure is therefore a harness/generated-output setup issue and does not demonstrate the claimed defect.

The hypothesis as constructed does not hold and cannot be fixed into a probe that distinguishes head from base. The premise that "a legitimate analyzer diagnostic deliberately created at Location.None" exists in this codebase is unverified: the changed paths (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull in H4, MemberNeedsKey in H5) both create diagnostics at member identifier locations, not Location.None, so no source member in the current compilation ever yields a Location.None diagnostic for C1's wrapper to drop. To exercise ReportIfLocatedInCompilation one would have to construct a diagnostic with Location.None by other means, which the analyzer does not do and the requirement does not ask for — so the broad-filtering concern is speculative rather than a defect the requirement covers. Additionally, the probe's failure at base and head with VerifyCS's generated-source-list mismatch shows the actual issue is harness setup (the test must use TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and proper verifier configuration as the change's own tests do), and even a corrected MsgPack004-on-source-member test would pass at both base and head because H5 preserves the source-member location — it cannot isolate the claimed regression. The stronger, requirement-relevant suspicion (H4's BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull branch and H1/H2 documentation not exercised) would be better probed, but this particular hypothesis (C1 silently drops legitimate Location.None diagnostics) is not supported by the code change and has no concrete source member that triggers it.

probes.title: README claim C4 is contradicted by analyzer running only in the consuming compilation
probes.hypothesis: C4 (and H1) claims diagnostics about metadata members are reported by the defining assembly. In practice the defining assembly is emitted as a library (no analyzer run) and may be a prebuilt NuGet package, so no assembly ever reports those member diagnostics. A test where the defining assembly's member is truly unattributed (no [MessagePackObject] but has an unattributed member reachable via the consumer) and the consumer compiles cleanly would pass — but a strict probe can demonstrate that a member of the metadata type with a BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull condition is not reported anywhere, contradicting the documentation. Under the claim, running the analyzer on the consumer alone should still surface something referring to the referenced member; it does not.
criteria: Running the MsgPack00x analyzer against the consumer-only compilation that references a metadata-only library whose member triggers BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull in the analyzer yields no diagnostic whose location is in consumer source but that describes the referenced member (item.Name from metadata).
probes.means: If the test PASSES it merely shows the consumer reports nothing for the metadata member, confirming C4/H1's documentation claim is untestably aspirational at best. If the assembly producing the metadata had been analyzed, a diagnostic would exist; the change provides no mechanism for that. This probe exposes that the documentation's premise is formulated without verification; the change's own tests (H8) also never exercise the metadata-member diagnostic path despite the claim it is reported by the defining assembly.

refusals.question: Is it intentional to suppress every TypeCollector analyzer diagnostic whose location is Location.None or outside the current compilation, rather than limiting the change to diagnostics for metadata members? This can also remove pre-existing compilation-level or otherwise source-less diagnostics unrelated to issue #2283.
refusals.why: This is an intentional diagnostic behavior change and may be broader than the crash fix; the owner must decide which diagnostics may now be dropped.
refusals.summary: Decide whether TypeCollector may suppress all non-source diagnostics beyond issue #2283

refusals.question: Is it acceptable that member diagnostics for a referenced binary can disappear entirely when its defining project was compiled without these analyzers, as can happen for a NuGet dependency or another prebuilt assembly?
refusals.why: The documentation and helper comment assume the defining compilation reports the problems, but nothing in the change guarantees that compilation ran the analyzer. Suppressing consumer diagnostics versus retaining or relocating them is a product behavior decision and an interpretation of the requirement.
refusals.summary: Decide whether consumer diagnostics may vanish for binaries without analyzers
